findings.claim: Bare var() inside type-ambiguous Tailwind arbitrary utilities (text-[var(--color-cyan)], border-[var(--color-signal-red)], focus-visible:outline-[var(--color-phosphor-glow)]) depends on Tailwind v4 namespace inference; if inferred as a length/width type the utility is silently dropped or misapplied, and none of the listed verification evidence inspects the emitted CSS.
findings.evidence: Diff hunks: `text-[var(--color-cyan)]` in enhanced-thread.tsx; `border-[var(--color-signal-red)]` and `focus-visible:outline-[var(--color-phosphor-glow)]` in error-bar.tsx. The acceptance criterion 'Runtime UX: colors, alpha, contrast, layout, focus, motion, and behavior remain visually equivalent' requires the focus outline to survive; verification.md lists only Vite dev compilation, typecheck, and lint, which do not assert that ambiguous arbitrary utilities were generated as colors.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Tailwind v4's explicit type-hinted variable shorthand (e.g. `text-(color:--color-cyan)`, `outline-(color:--color-phosphor-glow)`, `border-(color:--color-signal-red)`), or add a build-output grep asserting each new utility class produced a color declaration.

findings.claim: The scoped review patch still summarizes three of the fourteen index.css replacements: the hunk header claims 'shared brand and highlight theme (ten further replacements)' but enumerates only seven old/new pairs, so the packet cannot be fully verified against criterion 2.1's 14-site count.
findings.evidence: Diff: '@@ shared brand and highlight theme (ten further replacements)' followed by only seven replacement pairs (ember; surface+foreground; ember; cyan; fg-faint; foreground). The second adversarial review per verification.md blocked precisely because 'the scoped review patch summarized, rather than showed' real changes; three replacements in the highest-count file remain unshown.
findings.suggested_fix: Include the remaining three index.css old/new lines explicitly in the packet.

findings.claim: The deferred admin-page census is printed but never asserted, so criterion 3.4's 'prove the deferred admin-page set is untouched' rests entirely on a human reading one informational log line; any edit under frontend/src/admin/pages/ (additions or premature removals) passes the gate silently.
findings.evidence: `const deferredCount = ... .reduce(...)` is used only inside the final `console.log(...)`; there is no comparison, threshold, or drift warning. Task 3.4 reads 'Prove the migrated set is clean and the deferred admin-page set is untouched.'
findings.suggested_fix: Emit an explicit warning (non-blocking, to preserve C-14a freedom) when deferredCount differs from the last recorded census, e.g. 'deferred census drifted: expected ~307, got N'.

findings.claim: The success message hardcodes '29 non-admin call sites migrated' regardless of what was checked, and prints `null` for the deferred count when run in --fixture-file mode.
findings.evidence: `console.log(`HSL token codemod gate passed (29 non-admin call sites migrated; ${deferredCount} admin-page call sites currently deferred).`)` with `deferredCount = fixtureFile ? null : ...` — the count of actual remaining legacy sites is computed but never echoed, and the literal 29 will become stale.
findings.suggested_fix: Branch the success message for fixture mode, and derive the migrated claim from the computed violation count rather than a hardcoded constant.

findings.claim: The negative fixture only exercises the uppercase `HSL(` branch; the detector's advertised `hsla(var(` rejection (per design.md: 'rejects a remaining hsl(var( or hsla(var( sequence regardless of case') has no fixture coverage.
findings.evidence: scripts/fixtures/hsl-token-codemod/case-variant.tsx contains only `"HSL(var(--legacy-channel))"`; no fixture contains `hsla(` in any case, so a regression to /hsl\s*\(\s*var\s*\(/i would still pass the negative test.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a second fixture line or fixture file containing `hsla(var(--legacy-channel))` (and ideally an uppercase `HSLA(`) and assert both are rejected.

findings.claim: The gate verifies only the absence of legacy syntax, not the resolvability of the new semantic tokens, so a typo'd `--color-*` name would pass every listed gate (typecheck, lint, boundary, grep) while the browser silently drops the declaration.
findings.evidence: The detector is solely `/hsla?\s*\(\s*var\s*\(/gi` over six files; the migration introduces consumers of `--color-muted`, `--color-surface`, `--color-foreground`, `--color-ember`, `--color-cyan`, `--color-fg-faint` plus the five new terminal aliases, none of which are cross-checked against token definitions.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the gate to extract `var(--color-…)` references from the six files and assert each is defined in tokens.css or the terminal-theme block of index.css.
